text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT  GeoDNS failover churn detected. APAC-east edge resolvers returning intermittent CNAME loops and NXDOMAIN for `cdn.redwood.internal` and `api.redwood.example`. Paging oncall.

nina (oncall): ack. seeing a spike in client DNS timeouts + increased retries at edge LB. API error rate up ~1.9% in apac-east. I'll start digging into DNS traces and healthcheck events.

devon (network): running probes now. short cmds:
```
# dig @1.1.1.1 cdn.redwood.internal CNAME +short
cdn-primary.redwood.example.
# dig @203.119.91.5 cdn.redwood.internal CNAME +short
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> @203.119.91.5 cdn.redwood.internal CNAME +short
; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, rcode: NXDOMAIN

# aws route53 list-health-checks --query 'HealthChecks[?Name==`cdn-primary-hc`].{Id:Id,Status:HealthCheckConfig}'
```

devon (network): results: some public resolvers (Cloudflare apac cluster) intermittently see NXDOMAIN for the CNAME. Our authoritative zones show both primary and failover CNAMEs live. Route53 healthcheck logs show flapping for cdn-primary-hc around the same time.

lee (prod-sr): customers noticing increased 502/504s on large payload endpoints. Impact: CDN cache misses + origin retries. We have several enterprise customers in APAC; opening status.

nina (oncall): hypothesis: Route53 healthcheck flapping (maybe due to transient AZ networking) triggered GeoDNS failover to secondary, but secondary had an outdated CNAME pointing to deprecated alias, causing resolution loops or NXDOMAIN when resolvers query cached data. Need to confirm history and recent terraform deploys.

devon (network): checking terraform state & change history.

devon (network): found a change 9h ago: `geo_cname_rollover` applied to switch traffic for apac-east to `cdn-canary` with TTL=60. There was also a healthcheck threshold tightening 6h ago: consecutive-failures lowered from 3->1 (likely to detect flapping faster). That seems suspect.

nina (oncall): immediate mitigation options:
- revert healthcheck threshold to 3 (less sensitive)
- temporarily pin apac GeoDNS to a stable A records set (bypass CNAME failover) so resolvers resolve to IPs directly
- request Cloudflare to purge negative cache if they saw NXDOMAINs

ryan (sre): agree. quickest is revert threshold and pin to A records. Reverting Terraform for threshold is straightforward; pinning requires creating A-set in GeoDNS and applying.

nina (oncall): executing revert for healthcheck threshold.

nina (oncall): terraform plan/apply:
```
resource "aws_route53_health_check" "cdn_primary_hc" {
  failure_threshold = 3
}
```
apply complete.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: Route53 healthcheck config updated (change-id: chg-77543).

devon (network): preparing A record pin. creating short-lifetime A record set for apac-east with current healthy IPs.

devon (network): terraform snippet:
```
resource "redwood_geodns_record" "cdn_apac_pin" {
  region = "apac-east"
  ttl = 30
  type = "A"
  records = ["13.52.101.12","13.52.101.13"]
}
```
apply done.

support-bot: Cloudflare support ticket opened (CF-90901) with trace bundle; requested cache flush for apac resolvers.

(4m)

devon (network): external probes now returning A records from apac resolvers. NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL counts falling: 1.9% -> 0.3%.

lee (prod-sr): customer errors decreasing. Sending interim status: "Partial DNS resolution instability in APAC causing elevated API errors. Mitigation in progress; pinning edge to stable IPs and relaxing healthcheck sensitivity." Posting: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/RW-186999.

olga (sec): note: pinning to A records bypasses DNS-level failover; we must monitor origin health manually. Approve emergency exception for 45m?

ops-bot: sec-exception created: SEC-EX-2026-112. Auto-revert timer set to 45m.

nina (oncall): monitoring sweeps from multiple vantage points.

(10m pass)

devon (network): Cloudflare acknowledges ticket, purged negative cache for apac cluster. They also reported seeing rapid change in authoritative NS due to our GeoDNS rollouts, which explains cache thrash.

ryan (sre): adding a synthetic that performs resolver checks and cross-validates CNAME chains before we promote GeoDNS changes. Also propose adding a canary window longer than healthcheck threshold to prevent immediate flip for one-off blips.

lee (prod-sr): customer comms: update: mitigated, continued monitoring. Most customers restored, a few sessions may need retries. Postmortem scheduled.

(30m pass)

devon (network): auto-revert timer triggered; removing pinned A records and restoring original GeoDNS CNAME behavior. TTL low so resolvers should pick up change.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: geo-dns revert applied (plan-id: plan-99201).

nina (oncall): final checks: APAC resolver metrics stable, NXDOMAIN back to baseline. Error rates normalized.

olga (sec): recommend follow-ups: 1) revert healthcheck threshold change in deployment playbook, 2) require GeoDNS changes to not be gated by overly-sensitive healthchecks, 3) add preflight that verifies secondary CNAME targets are current.

ryan (sre): will own infra changes for GeoDNS canary process and add automated rollback conditions based on resolver observations.

lee (prod-sr): posting final status: INCIDENT RESOLVED. link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/RW-186999. Postmortem assigned to devon + ryan.

nina (oncall): leaving runbook entry in ops-playbook: steps to revert healthcheck, pin A records, contact CF, and monitor. Handing off to next oncall.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident archived at 1869999555.
